about.summary:
Hello. I'm Wonseok Shin, a fourth-year software engineer who has repeatedly worked on processing large volumes of data quickly and keeping data consistent as it moves through multiple systems. The domains differed — AI image generation, fintech, and spatial AI SaaS — but the problems I took on were mostly about processing performance and data consistency.

At Cupix, I am building a product that connects construction-site video data with BIM files containing building design information to track construction progress, and I own the work from feature spec review to data model, event flow, and API design. I cut the time to extract data from large BIM files with 1M+ objects from tens of minutes to a few minutes. I reworked the data pipeline so that 20M+ field data records and 100M+ snapshots and events stay consistent across 6+ regions.

Before that, I scaled an AI image generation service from a prototype to a production system handling 300K+ monthly requests while reducing GPU and CDN costs. At a fintech service, I introduced tests to inherited code that had none and raised coverage to about 70%, and in a Tibero environment with few DB tools, I automated local and CI test databases and released them as three open-source projects.

I believe the more systems a problem spans, the more likely a quick fix brings the same problem back. I want to work as an engineer who traces root causes to the end and turns them into solutions the team can apply right away.

experience.position: Backend Engineer / Application Part Lead · Backend
experience.description: A global spatial AI SaaS company that links 3D building design models (BIM) with 360° site captures to track construction progress and asset status. I work across a Rails monolith, NestJS and Lambda services, and 30+ processing agents.

achievements.title: BimAI (AI classification of BIM components)
details: Built and launched in 6 regions a NestJS service where AI suggests classifications for BIM components, replacing manual classification of hundreds of thousands of components in the browser
Detected intermittent OOM failures in large BIM extraction via a Datadog dashboard I had set up, mitigated them with a scale-up, then reworked extraction so large models finish in about 10 minutes
Cut 3D geometry download time from about 20 minutes to 3 by redesigning the legacy one-request-per-file download with parallel requests and WebSocket batching
Cut peak memory by about 70% by writing extracted objects to disk sequentially instead of holding them all in memory, and isolated extraction in a separate process to keep the API responsive

achievements.title: SiteInsights (construction progress analytics)
details: Designed a Kinesis event pipeline that keeps events in order per customer project, with a delivery worker and version guards, replacing 12 Lambda paths where events arrived out of order
Wrote a production-verified behavior spec from BIM registration to progress judgment, and built on it a MySQL/MongoDB consistency check API and a 120+ widget Datadog dashboard
Traced captures missing from analysis with six months of production data; added a reprocessing queue as a stopgap, then fixed the root cause by computing per capture instead of per date

achievements.title: Operations and incident response
details: Responded to a DB load spike by tracing a legacy path where one event fanned out into a flood of jobs, and fixed it with debouncing and a single UPDATE
Analyzed an incident where old instances queried a dropped column during a rolling deploy, and set a rule to split column removal across two deploys to prevent recurrence
Restored about 40,000 BIM components deleted by a customer upload mistake, using a recovery procedure with per-store completion criteria and pre-run checks

achievements.title: Application Part leadership
details: Led a 4-person part, owning quarterly goals and performance reviews; 98% of the 530+ items shipped during that period needed no rework after release
When review became the bottleneck after AI adoption, brought into the team review process an AI review that reads the diff, commits, and product specs and filters out unsupported comments
Built a knowledge setup where merged changes flow into per-service docs automatically, so AI coding tools also work from current context
Cut CI for the Rails monolith, which runs the full test suite before every deploy, from 49 to 12 minutes (76%) by slimming legacy factories that triggered dozens of DB writes per test record

experience.description: Standardized the team's Tibero-based development and test environment while taking over follow-up development, test coverage and query performance for a delivery mutual aid insurance back office.

achievements.title: Insurance back office
details: Joined a delayed back-office project for insurance staff late and delivered four contract features (quotation, payment, contract approval, endorsement) through QA
Introduced scenario-based characterization tests to untested inherited code, raising coverage in my area from 0% to about 70% as a regression safety net
Cut the first load of a ~5M-row contract list from 3.6s to 0.7s, and repeat loads of the same page to 0.2s with Redis and ETag
Reviewed execution plans for all SQL in my area and removed N+1 queries in list views with fetch joins and batch loading
Prevented lost updates when multiple staff endorsed the same contract with optimistic locking, verified by concurrent-save tests with zero lost updates

achievements.title: Tibero development environment
details: Automated local and CI test databases with a Tibero Docker image and a Testcontainers module, released as three open-source projects after internal validation
Built a Tibero dialect for Flyway, which had no Tibero support, automating DDL versioning and schema deployment
Shrank the Tibero Docker image by 70% (1.5GB to 401MB) with zstd compression and file cleanup

experience.description: Expanded MiriCanvas AI Drawing backend into production, from external AI model integrations to 300K+ monthly image generation requests and GPU/CDN cost optimization.

achievements.title: MiriCanvas AI Drawing
details: Scaled a prototype into a production system handling 300K+ image generation requests per month, with an asynchronous generation pipeline integrating OpenAI and Stability AI
Made generation idempotent with request-level identifiers so each request runs once across user retries, job reruns, and retries after external AI API failures

achievements.title: Infrastructure cost reduction
details: Analyzed GPU usage by resolution and model, then moved over-provisioned instances from g5.2xlarge to g5.xlarge, cutting GPU cost by 20% (about $185 per instance per month)
Cut GPU server setup time from 25 to 15 minutes by streamlining the spot instance AMI and model prewarming
Converted PNG to WebP in real time at the CloudFront response stage with Lambda@Edge, reducing average file size by 75% and CDN cost by about $450 per month without changing S3 storage
